questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Interior of a Set
questions.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,0\le {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}<4,\,0\le y<2}.
$$

The interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,,\,0<y<2}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072304/assets/f4ee8fbf9a7670a7d0e0b7488bccbf014f8db8fff0154c7db025f2b071aec566.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072304/assets/9fc733f6966b016c93b6ee6a305c5af5ee4fa432dad5d95e28061fd2a0d33efb.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,0<{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}<4,\,0<y<2}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying True Statements Regarding Interiors and Boundaries of Sets
questions.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}<36}.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $A$ contains none of its boundary points.
- $A$ contains some (not all) of its boundary points.
- $\text{int}\,A=A$
questions.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

In this case, the set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072304/assets/ff1f735266f66879834e02ca7601e90e40dfa7929e5796d4a3f8cb4ff2828de7.png)

  

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

Notice that, in this case, the set $A$ contains none of its boundary points. 

With that in mind, let's examine each statement:

- Statement I is true, while statement II is false. As we've seen, $A$ contains none of its boundary points.

- Statement III is true. Since $A$ contains none of its boundary points, we must have $\text{int}\,A=A.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

questions.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,1<{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}<4}.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?  

- $∂A\cap A\ne ∅$
- $\text{int}\,A\cap ∂A=∅$
- $A=\text{int}\,A$
questions.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

In this case, the set $A$ and its boundary $∂A={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072304/assets/2273cd843c4bfaeaff10d49d3400d7661262673639a66034638d805eef5b1e47.png)

   

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072304/assets/5e473584ef5193b434ff6c138b08c4fbd9111a37252019143b1afb2d48c913c6.png)

With that in mind, let's examine each statement:

- Statement I is false. As we've seen, $A$ contains none of its boundary points, so we must have  $∂A\cap A=∅.$

- Statement II is true. Since $\text{int}\,A$ contains all points in $A$ except the boundary points, we must have $\text{int}\,A\cap ∂A=∅,$ where $∅$ denotes the empty set.

- Statement III is true. Since $A$ contains none of its boundary points, we must have $A=\text{int}\,A.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III  only."
